intro: Look up at this granite needle. You are standing before the Obelisk of Theodosius, a monument in İstanbul province whose stone dates from the 15th century BC. Thutmose III raised it at Karnak; in AD 390 it was moved to the Hippodrome. Then look down: the reliefs on its base show, step by step, how it was set upright.
history: The obelisk's story begins at Karnak, where Pharaoh Thutmose III raised it in the fifteenth century BC. In the fourth century AD Constantius had it brought to Alexandria. Then, in 390, Theodosius I moved it to Constantinople and set it up on the spine of the Hippodrome. But the journey took its toll: it broke in transit, so only about a third of its original height stands today.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the granite shaft and its hieroglyphs, and the reliefs on the marble base. Then take in the Hippodrome spina and the Serpent Column beside it.
facts: Did you know? The reliefs on the marble base show the obelisk being raised with pulleys and ropes — an illustrated account of an ancient engineering operation. The stone was raised at Karnak in the fifteenth century BC and brought to Constantinople in AD 390, which makes it some two thousand years older than the city it stands in.
outro: This brings our tour of the Obelisk of Theodosius to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
